I ASKED Mr. Montgomery concerning the to-and-fro emergings of the people from the hooks and crannies of the hills and valleys and plains of this country—going and coming, so busily, everywhere, it would seem, with this new device called the automobile.

HOQUIAM, Nov. 4, (Special) —
The city commission found it impos-
sible to take final action on the milk
inspection measure, at its meeting
Wednesday, on account of the adoption
of an amendment including a clause
to license all trucks used for deliver-
ing milk. Commissioner G. F. Hill,
said to have been the stumbling block
to passage of the measure, declared
that he would not oppose passage of
the measure next week.

This measure has been before the
city commission for several months,
and the assurance was given to a
group of about 10 women, represent-
ing various women's clubs of Ho-
quiam, that final disposition would be
made at the next meeting. City
Attorney James P. H. Callahan ex-
plained that under the commission
form of government it was impossible
to pass any ordinance save in the
form in which it had been read at a
meeting one week previously. This
will give opportunity for the com-
mission to hear any views on the bill
in its final form, he said.

the funds applied by the county
to enforce it and similar ordinances
in other cities in the county, would
be inadequate, and said that a test-
ing laboratory as large as the library
building would be needed. The
women admitted that it might
not be entirely effective at first, but
said beginning was worth while, and
several cited instances to their per-
sonal knowledge, where situations had
been greatly improved.

When not on the Great Lakes with his nets on the trail of fish, Dr. Koel has spent many hours with trap and gun obtaining specimens of birds. He has gotten together and owns personally, one of the finest collections of hawks and waders in North America.

Scientists' Fishing Tackle

Going off to the Arctic to collect fish, birds and mammals is not like an afternoon's jaunt near home with gun or rod and line. Hundreds of pounds of special supplies and equipment had to be taken, and the problem of packing and transportation involved in getting specimens safely back to the United States had to be worked out. As Koel took aboard the Fearn, one of the MacMillan expedition ships, the following formidable supplies: 5 gallons of formaldehyde, 10 gallons of alcohol, 100 pounds of salt, 1000 feet of gill nets made of linen thread, rammed nets, dozens of thermometers, automatic water sampling bottles, silk, boiling cloth to seine up the almost microscopic food of the fish, dredges for creatures living on the sea bottom, insect nets, plant presses and a number of copper tanks for use in preserving fish.

Because space is at a high premium on the "Bowdoin" and "Arcary", there will be much importance on provision. When his fish have been "pickled" in alcohol and formaldehyde, Dr. Koel plans to commandeer empty gasoline drums in which to bring the specimens back to the United States. The fish are preserved whole, and will eventually repose in glass jars of alcohol.

Bird Skins Easy to Preserve

The preservation of bird specimens is simple. The skins are split and slipped off with the feathers still in place. The neck is then severed so that the head and skin remain. These are generously salted and after drying, are packed.

Charles W. Whittaker, state senator from Oliver county, has been arrested on charges of unlawfully cultivating state school lands and trespassing on school lands, Carl X. Kositzky, state land commissioner, said here today.

The charges were filed by Kositzky after Whittaker had ignored repeated demands that he pay the state for the use of the lands, the land commissioner said.

Smith, was 5000 feet over the sea at

away he would have been shot to
death.

observations, the target towed by the
plane showed four shrapnel holes.

fired 81 rounds.

company in Scranton, saved much
time while new telephone cable was
being installed between Scranton and
Philadelphia.
